title: Dollar Ends Week at Lowest Since May as Rate-Hike Bets Fade
summary: The dollar fell Friday after soft US labor data reduced expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates in the near term.

title: Innovation Doesn't Happen Without Crisis: Rolapp
summary: Brian Rolapp, CEO of PGA Tour, joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." They discuss the changing landscape of sports media coverage, the rising costs of streaming bills for consumers, and the evolution of the PGA Tour after the rise and fall of LIV Golf. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Once Upon a Farm CEO on Outlook Boost, Consumer Demand
summary: John Foraker, Co-Founder and CEO of Once Upon a Farm, discussed the company's strong 42% sales growth in the recent quarter and expressed confidence in sustaining this momentum due to resilient consumer demand across baby and kid food categories. The company has raised its guidance for the full year and anticipates continued growth. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Credit Card Balances at Pace with Inflation: Whitney
summary: Meredith Whitney, CEO of Meredith Whitney Advisory Group, joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." They discuss how many Americans are living payday to payday as well as how consumers are utilizing their credit cards. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: S&P 500 Has Best Week Since April After Jobs Data: Markets Wrap
summary: A sharp slowdown in the US jobs market drove stocks higher while bond yields fell on speculation the Federal Reserve won’t be forced to raise interest rates any time soon.

title: SpaceX Nears IPO Price Again After Staging $327 Billion Rally
summary: SpaceX shares jumped for a second straight day bringing them close to breaking back above the company’s $135 initial public offering price for the first time since falling below the key level last month.

title: US Army Wants to Let Companies Test Weapons Faster
summary: The US Army wants to see new weapons on the battlefield faster. Tyler Kendall sat down with US Army Secretary Dan Driscoll to discuss the Pentagon's plan to open up five military ranges to private industry.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Markets Rally on Weak Jobs Report | Closing Bell
summary: Comprehensive cross-platform coverage of the U.S. market close on Bloomberg Television, Bloomberg Radio, and YouTube with Romaine Bostick, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Wall Street Risk Complex Surges Anew Amid Deluge of Fresh Cash
summary: The financial world’s catalog of complaints keeps getting longer. In markets, however, the response is increasingly one of indifference.

title: US Stocks Rise After Jobs Data to Second-Best Week of the Year
summary: US stocks closed higher Friday after jobs data showed the US economy unexpectedly shed jobs in July, which could prompt the Federal Reserve to delay interest-rate increases.

title: Airbnb Jumps Most Since 2020 After Lifting Annual Outlook Again
summary: Airbnb Inc. had its biggest single-day stock rally in more than five years after boosting its annual revenue forecast for a second time this year.

title: This Spider-Man Is 'Deeper,' Say Sony's Rothman
summary: Sony Pictures Entertainment Motion Picture Group Chairman and CEO Tom Rothman says this latest Spider-Man movie was deeper and more emotional than others in the franchise.  He says "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" could be one of the studio's most profitable movies ever. Rothman also talks about ticket prices and making movies in California on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Taking Long Term Approach To Investing: Whitney
summary:
Meredith Whitney, CEO of Meredith Whitney Advisory Group, joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." They discuss Meredith's approach to personal investing and finance.
 (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Hedge Funds Slashed Yen Short Bets After US-Japan Joint Efforts
summary: Hedge funds sharply reduced bearish bets on the yen after coordinated efforts by US and Japanese officials helped stabilize the currency.

title: Short-Term Treasuries Cap Biggest Weekly Rally Since May on Data
summary: US Treasuries rallied after an unexpectedly weak July employment report prompted traders to further dial back expectations for Federal Reserve interest-rate hikes, cementing the biggest weekly gain in short-term maturities since May.

title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 7
summary: Oil steadied as tensions in the Middle East flared while traders monitored progress toward a deal between Iran and Oman to restore shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Gold Jumps as Weak US Jobs Data Adds Fuel to Bullion’s Rebound
summary: Gold jumped more than 3% after an unexpected contraction in the US jobs market, extending a rebound from its slump below $4,000 an ounce.

title: Investing View is Glass 'More Than Half-Full': Kelly
summary: David Kelly, Chief Global Strategist at JPMorgan Asset Management, joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." They discuss how biased information influences investor behavior.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: NYC Deputy Mayor on Jobs, Taxes, Grocery Stores
summary: Julie Su, New York City deputy mayor for economic justice, talks about creating jobs, a new business advisory council, city-run grocery stores and Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s new  pied-à-terre tax on second homes. More than 31,000 property owners may get a new bill in the mail. She speaks to Bloomberg's Romaine Bostick. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: US Sues Kahn on Hedge Fund Collapse, Indicts Executive
summary: The US Securities and Exchange Commission sued Brian Kahn, the former head of Franchise Group Inc., over the collapse of a hedge fund that he helped run, and federal prosecutors criminally charged an executive at the fund in the matter.
